active_problem.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1,200-1,260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07).
Manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target across 9,200 manual-read accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-01).
Ticket response times are already within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d), contradicting the requester's response-speed framing (E-02).
A majority (59%) of disputed bills are ACTUAL-read rather than ESTIMATED-read (E-03), so the identified mechanism does not explain most disputes.
active_problem.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1,200-1,260/month (Aug-Sep 2026, E-07), with the surge onset coinciding with manual-read route completion falling to 88% against a 95% target across 9,200 manual-read accounts in Aug-Sep (E-01). Missed manual reads trigger estimate substitution in the billing-import step of the meter-to-cash process, and estimated bills are a documented driver of disputes (1,240 of 3,025 disputed bills, 41%, are ESTIMATED-read, E-03), making the manual-read route-completion shortfall the best-evidenced contributing cause of the dispute surge among the hypotheses tested. This mechanism does not account for the ACTUAL-read majority of disputed bills (59%, E-03), which remains an open question, and ticket response times are already within the 3.0-day SLA (E-02), ruling out the requester's response-automation framing as the fix.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-log record shows manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 ran at 88%, seven points below the 95% target, across 9200 manual-read accounts, indicating a measurable shortfall in field read collection during the dispute-surge window.

The observation shows CRM dispute ticket response times (2,440 tickets, median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are already within the 3.0-day SLA, indicating the dispute surge is not primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem as the requester's framing suggests.

The billing-db disputed_bills_by_read_type query (E-03) shows 1,785 of 3,025 disputed bills (59%) are ACTUAL-read bills versus 1,240 (41%) ESTIMATED-read bills, meaning disputes are not predominantly tied to estimate substitution and most disputed bills were built from reads that were actually received, not estimated.

The billing-db tariff_change_log query returned zero records, meaning no tariff change was logged in the system of record during the review period. This rules out a tariff change as the mechanism behind the "non-error" explanation of the dispute surge.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims manual-read routes have run late since July due to being short three readers, and that affected customers receive estimated bills as a result; this is an unverified stakeholder claim offering a causal mechanism for the route-completion shortfall already observed in E-01, not new tool evidence. SH-FIELD's stated incentive (contract headcount increase) and documented bias (attributes problems to staffing) mean this narrative needs independent corroboration before being treated as established cause.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year; this stakeholder claim corroborates E-04's authoritative tool finding of zero tariff-change-log records, further weakening a tariff-change explanation for the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-log record shows manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 ran at 88%, seven points below the 95% target, across 9200 manual-read accounts, indicating a measurable shortfall in field read collection during the dispute-surge window.

The observation shows CRM dispute ticket response times (2,440 tickets, median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are already within the 3.0-day SLA, indicating the dispute surge is not primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem as the requester's framing suggests.

The billing-db disputed_bills_by_read_type query (E-03) shows 1,785 of 3,025 disputed bills (59%) are ACTUAL-read bills versus 1,240 (41%) ESTIMATED-read bills, meaning disputes are not predominantly tied to estimate substitution and most disputed bills were built from reads that were actually received, not estimated.

The billing-db counts (1,240 ESTIMATED vs 1,785 ACTUAL disputed bills) still stand as observed. The ESTIMATED subset no longer means missed manual reads triggered estimate substitution: E-10 shows this subset's reads are all AMI-channel, rejected at import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) or missing on AMI, not tied to manual-read route completion as the root problem's chain assumed.

The billing-db tariff_change_log query returned zero records, meaning no tariff change was logged in the system of record during the review period. This rules out a tariff change as the mechanism behind the "non-error" explanation of the dispute surge.

SH-FIELD's stated incentive (contract headcount increase) and documented bias (attributes problems to staffing) mean this narrative needs independent corroboration before being treated as established cause.

The stakeholder quote still accurately records SH-FIELD's claim of a staffing shortage since July causing late routes and estimated bills. It no longer plausibly explains the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputes: E-10 shows those bills' AMI reads were either rejected at import or never received, a cause unrelated to field staffing or manual-read route lateness.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year; this stakeholder claim corroborates E-04's authoritative tool finding of zero tariff-change-log records, further weakening a tariff-change explanation for the dispute surge.

The surge onset is August, one month after SH-FIELD's claimed staffing shortage "since July," since July volume (590) is not elevated relative to June (610).

release_summary.summary: The problem started as SH-CS's claim (CL-01) that dispute tickets doubled since August and needed an auto-answering/auto-fixing AI agent. Investigation (E-07) confirmed the doubling (610/590 to 1,180/1,260 per month) but showed response times are already within SLA (E-02), ruling out the requested automation framing. An initial causal theory (PD-1@v1: route-completion shortfall plus field staffing, E-01/E-05) was invalidated once E-10 revealed the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills' AMI reads were rejected at import or never received, unrelated to route completion. The successor problem (PD-1@v2) establishes that billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit conversion (E-11), misflags firmware v4.2 meters reporting in 0.1 m3 units (E-12) as high-consumption, driving 1,184 of 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputes (E-10/E-13/E-14/E-15). This explains 41% of disputes but not the 59% ACTUAL-read majority (E-03), which stays an open unknown. The release decision is HOLD: nothing has been released. The hold reasons are that a Layer 1 safety-predicate/verification check failed, with 1,190 items of required escalation_billing_evidence reported missing, and that this verification could not be established. Two BEFORE_RELEASE verification obligations (on the ACTUAL-read dispute cause and the full firmware-v4.2 population scope) remain OPEN, so related work is excluded from this release. Planned remediation work escalating BV-17 evidence to SH-BILL is partly done, but packaging and release-blocking verification steps are still pending.
key_points: The original request from SH-CS ("build an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and fixes wrong bills") was treated as a claim (CL-01) to test, not the problem itself.

Dispute volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1,180-1,260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) per E-07/F-05. Response times are already within SLA (E-02/F-02), rejecting the response-automation framing (H-SLOW-RESPONSE-AUTOMATION-GAP: REJECTED).

An initial problem definition (PD-1@v1) attributed the surge to a manual-read route-completion shortfall (E-01, 88% vs 95% target) and field staffing (E-05, SH-FIELD claim), but this was INVALIDATED when E-10 showed the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills' AMI reads were either rejected at import (1,184) or never received (56) - a mechanism unrelated to route completion.

The successor problem definition PD-1@v2 (CONDITIONAL_PASS) establishes the root cause as billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-11), misflagging firmware v4.2 meters that report in 0.1 m3 units instead of m3 (E-12) as high-consumption, causing 1,184 of 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputes to be rejected and estimate-substituted (E-10, E-13, E-14, E-15 corroborate).

This BV-17/firmware-unit mechanism explains the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputes (41% of all disputes) but does NOT explain the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputes (59% majority, E-03), which remains an open unknown (U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE).

The release decision is HOLD: nothing was released. The hold reasons are (1) 1,190 items of escalation_billing_evidence were missing per the Layer 1 verification check (recent_events seq 336), and (2) the required safety predicate/verification was not established.

Two verification obligations required BEFORE_RELEASE are still OPEN and block expanded scope: VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE (the ACTUAL-read dispute majority cause) and VOB-U-FIRMWARE-POPULATION-SCOPE (total v4.2 accounts potentially affected beyond the 1,240 already disputed).

Planned work items for escalating the BV-17/firmware evidence to SH-BILL (W-ESCALATE-BILLING-EVIDENCE, W-ESCALATE-AMI-EVIDENCE) are marked DONE, but the packaging step (W-COMPILE-ESCALATION-PACKET) and dispute-volume monitoring packaging (W-MONITOR-DISPUTE-VOLUME) are still PENDING, and the release-blocking verification item (W-VERIFY) is PENDING.
limitations_explained: The actual fix for BV-17 (SR-FIX-BV17-UNIT-SCALING, converting raw register values to m3 before comparison) is judged not feasible within the contest time budget, so misflagging/rejection of firmware v4.2 reads continues until it ships and is independently verified.

The 56 disputed accounts with NO_READ_RECEIVED (distinct from the 1,184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION cases) have not been investigated; it is unknown whether this is a vendor export/delivery gap via ORG-AMI/H-MDMS-BILL, separate from the BV-17 defect.

Scope items diagnose_firmware_rollout_scope:DA-MDMS and analyze_actual_read_disputes:DA-BILL are excluded from this release because their corresponding verification obligations (VOB-U-FIRMWARE-POPULATION-SCOPE and VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE) are OPEN and required BEFORE_RELEASE.

Even if everything in the current release scope were completed, it would not restore dispute volume to the pre-August baseline (goal G-1), because it does not address the 59% ACTUAL-read dispute majority or the 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED cases.
Dispute ticket response-time automation is explicitly not a target of this remediation and does not address the identified root cause, since response times are already within SLA (E-02).
mdms-export tool health and billing-config reliability for any future expanded scope remain only partially characterized, per the design's stated limitation.

No automated bill writes are proposed or permitted in any case, per constraint K-BILLWRITE (Billing Operations authority required for all bill adjustments); the design's own success criterion SC-NO-AUTOMATED-BILL-WRITES reflects this.

Several supporting assumptions behind the earlier causal story (A-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-LINKS-DISPUT, A-STAFFING-CAUSES-SHORTFALL, A-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-APPLIE) are now INVALIDATED by E-10, underscoring that stakeholder claims (e.g., SH-FIELD's staffing narrative, E-05) were leads, not established facts.

key_points: The original request from SH-CS ("build an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and fixes wrong bills") was treated as a claim (CL-01) to test, not the problem itself.

Dispute volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1,180-1,260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) per E-07/F-05. Response times are already within SLA (E-02/F-02), rejecting the response-automation framing (H-SLOW-RESPONSE-AUTOMATION-GAP: REJECTED).

An initial problem definition (PD-1@v1) attributed the surge to a manual-read route-completion shortfall (E-01, 88% vs 95% target) and field staffing (E-05, SH-FIELD claim), but this was INVALIDATED when E-10 showed the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills' AMI reads were either rejected at import (1,184) or never received (56) - a mechanism unrelated to route completion.

The successor problem definition PD-1@v2 (CONDITIONAL_PASS) establishes the root cause as billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-11), misflagging firmware v4.2 meters that report in 0.1 m3 units instead of m3 (E-12) as high-consumption, causing 1,184 of 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputes to be rejected and estimate-substituted (E-10, E-13, E-14, E-15 corroborate).

This BV-17/firmware-unit mechanism explains the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputes (41% of all disputes) but does NOT explain the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputes (59% majority, E-03), which remains an open unknown (U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE).

The release decision is HOLD: nothing was released. The hold reasons are (1) 1,190 items of escalation_billing_evidence were missing per the Layer 1 verification check (recent_events seq 336), and (2) the required safety predicate/verification was not established.

Two verification obligations required BEFORE_RELEASE are still OPEN and block expanded scope: VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE (the ACTUAL-read dispute majority cause) and VOB-U-FIRMWARE-POPULATION-SCOPE (total v4.2 accounts potentially affected beyond the 1,240 already disputed).

Planned work items for escalating the BV-17/firmware evidence to SH-BILL (W-ESCALATE-BILLING-EVIDENCE, W-ESCALATE-AMI-EVIDENCE) are marked DONE, but the packaging step (W-COMPILE-ESCALATION-PACKET) and dispute-volume monitoring packaging (W-MONITOR-DISPUTE-VOLUME) are still PENDING, and the release-blocking verification item (W-VERIFY) is PENDING.
limitations_explained: The actual fix for BV-17 (SR-FIX-BV17-UNIT-SCALING, converting raw register values to m3 before comparison) is judged not feasible within the contest time budget, so misflagging/rejection of firmware v4.2 reads continues until it ships and is independently verified.

The 56 disputed accounts with NO_READ_RECEIVED (distinct from the 1,184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION cases) have not been investigated; it is unknown whether this is a vendor export/delivery gap via ORG-AMI/H-MDMS-BILL, separate from the BV-17 defect.

Scope items diagnose_firmware_rollout_scope:DA-MDMS and analyze_actual_read_disputes:DA-BILL are excluded from this release because their corresponding verification obligations (VOB-U-FIRMWARE-POPULATION-SCOPE and VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE) are OPEN and required BEFORE_RELEASE.

Even if everything in the current release scope were completed, it would not restore dispute volume to the pre-August baseline (goal G-1), because it does not address the 59% ACTUAL-read dispute majority or the 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED cases.
Dispute ticket response-time automation is explicitly not a target of this remediation and does not address the identified root cause, since response times are already within SLA (E-02).
mdms-export tool health and billing-config reliability for any future expanded scope remain only partially characterized, per the design's stated limitation.

No automated bill writes are proposed or permitted in any case, per constraint K-BILLWRITE (Billing Operations authority required for all bill adjustments); the design's own success criterion SC-NO-AUTOMATED-BILL-WRITES reflects this.

Several supporting assumptions behind the earlier causal story (A-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-LINKS-DISPUT, A-STAFFING-CAUSES-SHORTFALL, A-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-APPLIE) are now INVALIDATED by E-10, underscoring that stakeholder claims (e.g., SH-FIELD's staffing narrative, E-05) were leads, not established facts.
output.summary: The problem started as SH-CS's claim (CL-01) that dispute tickets doubled since August and needed an auto-answering/auto-fixing AI agent. Investigation (E-07) confirmed the doubling (610/590 to 1,180/1,260 per month) but showed response times are already within SLA (E-02), ruling out the requested automation framing. An initial causal theory (PD-1@v1: route-completion shortfall plus field staffing, E-01/E-05) was invalidated once E-10 revealed the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills' AMI reads were rejected at import or never received, unrelated to route completion. The successor problem (PD-1@v2) establishes that billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit conversion (E-11), misflags firmware v4.2 meters reporting in 0.1 m3 units (E-12) as high-consumption, driving 1,184 of 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputes (E-10/E-13/E-14/E-15). This explains 41% of disputes but not the 59% ACTUAL-read majority (E-03), which stays an open unknown. The release decision is HOLD: nothing has been released. The hold reasons are that a Layer 1 safety-predicate/verification check failed, with 1,190 items of required escalation_billing_evidence reported missing, and that this verification could not be established. Two BEFORE_RELEASE verification obligations (on the ACTUAL-read dispute cause and the full firmware-v4.2 population scope) remain OPEN, so related work is excluded from this release. Planned remediation work escalating BV-17 evidence to SH-BILL is partly done, but packaging and release-blocking verification steps are still pending.
